questions.q: What is an independent variable in an experimental design?
a: The variable that is deliberately changed or manipulated by the investigator
The variable that is measured as the outcome
A factor that must be kept strictly constant
The random error in data collection

questions.q: What is a dependent variable?
a: The variable changed on purpose by the scientist
The variable that is measured to see the effect of changing the independent variable
A factor kept constant throughout all trials
The equipment used to conduct the test

questions.q: What are controlled variables (constant variables)?
a: Variables that are altered randomly during the experiment
Variables that measure the final outcome
All other factors that could affect the dependent variable which must be kept constant to ensure a fair test
Errors made during data recording

questions.q: Why is it essential to keep all controlled variables constant in a biological experiment?
a: To make the laboratory report look longer
To ensure the equipment does not overheat
To prevent accidents with glassware
To ensure that any change in the dependent variable is caused solely by the independent variable, making the test fair

questions.q: In an investigation testing the effect of different temperatures on enzyme amylase activity, what is the independent variable?
a: Temperature
Rate of starch breakdown
Concentration of amylase solution
pH level

questions.q: In an investigation testing how light intensity affects the rate of photosynthesis in pondweed, what is the dependent variable?
a: Distance of the lamp from the pondweed
Rate of photosynthesis (measured by oxygen bubbles counted or volume collected per minute)
Color of the pondweed leaves
Temperature of the water bath

questions.q: When designing an experiment to investigate osmosis using potato cylinders in varying sucrose concentrations, which factor should be controlled?
a: The concentration of the sucrose solutions
The initial mass and surface area of the potato cylinders
The final mass of the potato cylinders
The type of sugar used

questions.q: What is the purpose of a control setup in an enzyme experiment where boiled enzyme is used instead of active enzyme?
a: To speed up the chemical reaction
To measure room temperature accurately
To provide extra substrate molecules
To prove that the active enzyme protein is necessary for the reaction and that heat denaturation stops activity

questions.q: What is a hypothesis in scientific experimental design?
a: A proposed testable explanation for a phenomenon or observation, often written as a prediction
A proven mathematical law that never changes
A list of apparatus required for a practical
The final conclusion written after an experiment

questions.q: How can an investigator ensure that an experiment yields reliable (consistent) results?
a: By changing multiple independent variables at the same time
By repeating the experiment multiple times under identical conditions and calculating means
By altering the control variables during the test
By ignoring anomalous data points without checking

questions.q: Which of the following describes a 'fair test'?
a: An experiment where no measurements are recorded
An experiment where multiple independent variables change simultaneously
An experiment where only one independent variable is changed while all other potential variables are rigorously controlled
An experiment conducted outdoors in natural sunlight

questions.q: Why do scientists include a wide range of values for the independent variable (e.g., testing 5 different temperatures: 10, 20, 30, 40, and 50 °C) instead of just two?
a: To use up all available chemical reagents
To make calculations more difficult
To test student math skills
To allow any trends, optimum points, or turning points in the data to be clearly identified on a graph

questions.q: What is the role of preliminary trials (pilot studies) in experimental design?
a: To test the procedure, identify practical difficulties, and determine a suitable range of values for the independent variable
To write the final examination paper
To replace the main experiment entirely
To dispose of hazardous chemical waste

questions.q: When investigating the effect of pH on pepsin enzyme activity, what must be used to maintain specific pH levels?
a: Pure distilled water only
Buffer solutions of different pH values
Concentrated hydrochloric acid in all tubes
Universal indicator paper dipped continuously

questions.q: In an experiment testing seed germination requirements, why are seeds placed in petri dishes with damp cotton wool rather than soaked completely under deep water?
a: To keep the seeds warm
To prevent seeds from growing too tall
To ensure an adequate supply of oxygen for aerobic respiration during germination
To stop light from reaching the radicle

questions.q: What does a risk assessment in experimental design involve?
a: Calculating the financial cost of glassware
Estimating the student grade average
Predicting the exact numerical result of the test
Identifying potential hazards (e.g., hot water, corrosive acids, sharp scalpels) and specifying safety precautions to minimize harm

questions.q: If an investigator wants to test the effect of surface area on the rate of agar cube diffusion, what should be varied?
a: The size (dimensions) of the agar blocks
The temperature of the room
The concentration of hydrochloric acid
The color of the indicator

questions.q: What is a limitation in experimental design?
a: The number of pages in a notebook
A restriction or flaw in the method or equipment that restricts the precision or scope of the conclusions
The name of the student performing the practical
The bright lighting in the laboratory

questions.q: When designing an experiment to measure human reaction time, which factor should be controlled to ensure fair comparison between participants?
a: The age and gender of every person tested
The time of day, resting state, and method of dropping the ruler
The color of the ruler used
The room humidity level

questions.q: Why is it important to state the units of variables clearly in experimental planning?
a: To make the report look colorful
To confuse rival scientists
To fulfill grammar rules
To ensure clarity and allow correct mathematical processing and graph plotting

questions.q: What is the primary characteristic of a well-designed biological investigation?
a: It has a clear hypothesis, a single changing independent variable, a measured dependent variable, and tightly controlled extraneous variables
It uses the most expensive electronic equipment available
It avoids taking numerical measurements entirely
It takes less than five minutes to complete

questions.q: How can an investigator test whether carbon dioxide is necessary for photosynthesis in a leaf?
a: Place the plant in a dark cupboard for a week
Use soda lime in a sealed bell jar to absorb carbon dioxide as a control treatment alongside a normal control plant
Boil the leaf in alcohol immediately
Add glucose solution to the soil

questions.q: What is an extraneous variable?
a: The main independent variable being tested
The final calculated mean value
Any variable other than the independent variable that could influence the dependent variable if not controlled
The title of the practical report

questions.q: When planning an investigation into anaerobic respiration in yeast, why is a layer of liquid paraffin or oil often poured on top of the glucose-yeast mixture?
a: To feed the yeast extra nutrients
To heat the mixture evenly
To prevent gas bubbles from escaping
To prevent oxygen from entering, ensuring anaerobic conditions are maintained

questions.q: What is meant by the reproducibility of an experiment?
a: The ability of other researchers to obtain similar results using the same general method in different laboratories
Getting the exact same number every single time
Memorizing the practical steps word for word
Drawing diagrams without a ruler

questions.q: What is repeatability in experimental work?
a: Changing the independent variable every minute
The closeness of agreement between successive measurements obtained by the same person using the same method under the same conditions
The total number of test tubes used
The speed at which data is written down

questions.q: In an experiment investigating vitamin C content in fruit juices by titration with DCPIP, what factor must be kept constant to ensure valid comparison?
a: The volume and concentration of the DCPIP solution used in each test
The color of the fruit juice bottles
The brand of the burette clamp
The temperature of the laboratory lighting

questions.q: Why should an experimental method be written in a sequential, numbered, or step-by-step format?
a: To test artistic drawing skills
To confuse students reading it
To make the report look neat
To allow someone else to follow the exact procedure and replicate the investigation successfully
